title: BroadcastChannel (and MessagePort) implicitly call for dispatched events to not be trusted, but browsers mark them as trusted and they should be trusted
body:
Both of these sections call for creating an event but do not specify that it should be trusted.  The DOM spec that they depend on call for the event to not be trusted unless otherwise specified.  Either the HTML spec should be amended in its constructions of the event or the DOM Event spec updated to more explicitly depend on the method of dispatch:

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#transferMessagePort

> Create an event e that uses the MessageEvent interface, with the name message, which does not bubble and is not cancelable. The data attribute must be initialised to messageClone and the ports attribute must be initialised to newPorts.

and

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/comms.html#broadcasting-to-other-browsing-contexts

> Create an event e that uses the MessageEvent interface, with the event type message, which does not bubble and is not cancelable. The data attribute must be initialised to StructuredClone(clonedMessage, targetRealm) and the origin attribute must be initialised to the Unicode serialisation of sourceSettings's origin.

Initially raised for Firefox in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1288935 with things changing slightly as of today because https://github.com/whatwg/html/commit/ee103bbdba81bdbb8eb8e1bf77e9565f6158c5be removed the language that explicitly called for the BroadcastChannel event to be "not trusted" (and the MessagePort case left unspecified and thus falling through to the DOM spec.)

The WHATWG DOM normative spec definition of isTrusted is: "The isTrusted
attribute must return the value it was initialized to. When an event is created the attribute must be initialized to false." (https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-istrusted)  The note above that for isTrusted is currently as follows:  "Returns true if event was dispatched by the user agent, and false otherwise." but again is non-normative.

Firefox/Gecko currently explicitly sets the event to trusted in both cases where it constructs the MessagePort and BroadcastChannel events for dispatch.  Chromium seems to set things trusted exclusively based on their dispatch mechanism, but I could be misreading things.  Citations at https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1288935#c7

cc @annevk
